citations.texte: Finally, another important factor is the quality of bracing. There is good agreement to judge it according to the in-brace correction [136:537–45.") , 210:1343–52.") , 212:201–7.") , 229 , 230 , 231 , 232 , 233 , 234 ], even though the currently reported percentages of correction, showed a significant variability from 20 to 25% to 40–50%. Furthermore, the in brace correction is considered as prognostic factors for final good results and it has become, on one hand, the starting point to develop new braces [85 concept. Scoliosis. 2011;6:8.") , 202 , 203 , 235 , 236 , 237 , 237 , 238 , 239:180–5.") ] and, on the other, a biomechanical reference for various studies [232:1706–13.") , 239 , 240 , 241:339–44.") ]. Recently, a finite element model study confirmed the importance of immediate in-brace correction to predict long-term outcome of bracing treatment [242:369–76.") ]. Other factors such as the absolute reduction of the Cobb angle (i.e. in rigid curves over 50°) or 3D correction might also be important and should be considered in the future [243:185–90.") ]: in fact, it is still possible that a great in-brace reduction corresponds to a worsening of other parameters, e.g. in the sagittal plane, finally driving to a flat-back and worse functional results [133 , 146:213–20.") ] . In this respect, it is mandatory not to confuse the in-brace correction with the success of an orthotic treatment. While in-brace correction studies should be considered preliminary, only results at the end of treatment and/or at minimum of 1–2 years post treatment follow-up should be regarded as proof of efficacy. In any case, according to the actual knowledge, in-brace correction should be regarded as a way to individually judge the quality of the brace applied to single patients.

citations.texte: Adherence to treatment is the second main issue to be considered. Many studies have underlined that reported compliance is correlated with final results [106 , 207:1957–63.") , 210:1343–52.") , 212:201–7.") , 213:151–8.") ]. Compliance to bracing has been correlated to quality of life and psychological issues [174:57–63.") , 214 , 215 , 216 , 217:257–61.") ]. Since patients during clinical evaluations overstate their adherence to treatment [218:143–6.") ], heat sensors have been developed to check real compliance: it has been confirmed that both reported and estimated hours of brace wearing are inaccurate 218 , 219 , 220 , 221 , 222 , 223 , [224:59–73.") ] and that compliance is not correlated with the hours of bracing prescribed [223:2070–4. discussion 2074") ]. Nighttime wear is more accepted than daytime [225:2243–50. discussion 2250–1") ], and a “dose-response” to bracing seems to be confirmed [210:1343–52.") , 226:343–7.") ]. It has also been proposed that it is possible to develop a progression model in single patients with a formula including the risk of progression at the beginning of brace treatment, plus the use in terms of brace tightness and wear time [222 ]. It is clear that, since patients are not fully compliant, bracing appears not effective. SOSORT propose that compliance should be considered in terms of management of patients: in this perspective, adherence to treatment is a characteristic neither of the treatment only, nor of the patient alone, but of the good interaction between these two factors, based on the active approach by an expert treatment team able to reduce the burden of the brace and increase the coping abilities of the patient [135. Guidelines on “standards of management of idiopathic scoliosis with corrective braces in everyday clinics and in clinical research”: SOSORT consensus 2008. Scoliosis. 2009;4:2.") , 227:107–11.") ]. A setting with great attention to the patient and his family and a team approach is able to enhance compliance, thus allowing very good adherence even with fulltime brace wear as demonstrated by research based on the use of compliance monitor [228:12.") ]. Mainly for these reasons, SOSORT proposes its recommendations [120 ].

Dans l’essai cité, le but évalué était d’éviter la progression vers le domaine chirurgical, défini par un Cobb ≥ 50°audit-dx1-sosort-but-chiffre. Le succès atteignait 72% sous corset contre 48% sous observation ; ces résultats ne garantissent donc pas une réussite individuelle uniformeeu-sosort-2018-92. Ce seuil définit l’événement étudié ; il ne remplace donc pas l’individualisation clinique selon la courbure, l’âge et la maturitéeu-sosort-2018-155.
Une bonne correction sous orthèse renseigne la qualité technique ; elle ne doit cependant pas être confondue avec la réussite finaleeu-sosort-2018-111. L'objectif est donc suivi dans le temps, avec la morphologie, les paramètres fonctionnels et l'adhésioneu-sosort-2018-111eu-sosort-2018-242eu-sosort-2018-110.

11.B Les moyens conservateurs sont choisis selon la situation clinique

L'observation comprend un suivi clinique régulier ; elle ne signifie donc pas un abandon de la trajectoire évolutiveprep-dx1-observation. Une SIA modérée de plus de 20° avec croissance résiduelle peut relever de l'association corset et physiothérapie décrite par la source suisseprep-sia23-corset.
Le est intégré à une prise en charge d'équipe, avec adaptation, contrôle de qualité et attention portée à l'adhésionprep-dx1-equipeeu-sosort-2018-107eu-sosort-2018-111. Ainsi, le résultat dépend de plusieurs composantes de traitement, et non du seul fait de posséder une orthèseeu-sosort-2018-107.
L'orthèse est un moyen de contrôle de progression
Le but principal du corset est l'arrêt de progression ; la source suisse l'associe à la physiothérapie dans les conditions de courbure et de croissance décritespa17-sosortmechan-corsetprep-sia23-corset. La correction pendant le port renseigne la qualité technique, mais ne démontre pas à elle seule une réussite durableeu-sosort-2018-111. L'équipe apprécie donc l'usage réel, la tolérance et l'évolution au fil du suivieu-sosort-2018-110eu-sosort-2018-111.
Les exercices spécifiques comprennent des approches d'autocorrection intrinsèque ou assistée ; leur choix ne se confond donc pas avec une activité physique quelconqueeu-sosort-2018-155. Les essais rapportés montrent des effets possibles sur l'angle, l'endurance et certains domaines de qualité de vieeu-sosort-2018-168.
L'activité sportive reste distinguée d'un programme thérapeutique spécifique ; une association épidémiologique ne prouve pas un effet causal ou correcteureu-sosort-2018-191eu-sosort-2018-192. La natation ne doit donc pas être présentée comme une cause démontrée de scoliose sur la seule base des associations citéeseu-sosort-2018-192.

11.B.1 L'adhésion est soutenue avec l'adolescent et sa famille

L'éducation, l'évaluation psychologique, la surveillance des résultats et l'ajustement du traitement participent à la prise en charge conservatriceprep-dx1-education. L'équipe peut comprendre médecin, physiothérapeute, orthésiste et psychologue ; les responsabilités se coordonnent donc autour du patientprep-dx1-equipe.
Les heures déclarées de port peuvent différer de l'usage réel ; les études ont donc utilisé des moyens de mesure pour mieux apprécier l'adhésioneu-sosort-2018-110. Une difficulté de port est discutée comme une interaction entre traitement et vécu du patient, plutôt qu'une faute personnelle isoléeeu-sosort-2018-110.
La famille et l'équipe peuvent faciliter l'adaptation au traitement ; le soutien est ainsi intégré à la qualité de la prescriptioneu-sosort-2018-110prep-dx1-equipe. Une aggravation appelle une réévaluation du risque, de la correction et de l'usage effectif, plutôt qu'un changement automatique fondé sur un seul paramètreeu-sosort-2018-107eu-sosort-2018-111eu-sosort-2018-155.

11.B.2 Une conduite urgente reste indépendante du calendrier orthopédique

Si une rétention urinaire, une anesthésie en selle ou d'autres signaux neurologiques d'alarme apparaissent, une imagerie est réalisée sans attendre avec avis neurochirurgicalpa17-lomb22-queuepa17-lomb22-urgence. Le prochain contrôle de scoliose ne constitue donc pas l'échéance adaptée à cette situationpa17-lomb22-urgence.
Si une infection vertébrale ou péridurale est suspectée sur les signes et le terrain, l'IRM urgente suit cette branche spécifiquepa17-lomb22-infectionpa17-lomb22-irm-infection. Une douleur ou un déficit nouveau n'est donc pas géré uniquement par une modification d'exercices ou de corsetpa17-lomb22-urgencepa17-lomb22-irm-infection.

Urgence — conduite chronologique

D’abord, le clinicien identifie déficit d’alarme, rétention, anesthésie en selle ou autres signes neurologiques nouveaux.pa17-lomb22-queuepa17-lomb22-urgence

11.C La surveillance combine clinique, croissance et imagerie pertinente

La surveillance recherche une évolution morphologique et fonctionnelle ; elle intègre le risque lié à la croissance et au type de courbureeu-sosort-2018-155eu-sosort-2018-242. Dans la SIA sans indication de corset, la source suisse donne un cadre général de contrôle radiologique non réalisé avant 6 mois pour rechercher une progressionprep-sia23-suivi. Cependant, elle décrit aussi une phase critique liée à l'année avant et après la ménarchedx1-sia23-periode-critique.

11.D Le pronostic se juge au-delà de la correction immédiate

Le potentiel évolutif diminue après la fin de croissance, tandis que certaines grandes courbures gardent une progression adulte probablepa17-sosort-risqueeu-sosort-2018-17. The exercises publications have been tentatively classified according to the auto-correction proposed [272:451–5.") ]: extrinsic (maximal correction obtained also with the help of gravity, positioning devices and/or limbs placement) [88:1204–14.") , 190:209–14.") , 192: an age- and sex-matched controlled study. Pediatr Rehabil. 2003;6(1):23–30.") , 269:1429–35.") , 277 , 278 , 279 , 280 , 282:395–406.") , 283 ], intrinsic (maximal correction achievable without any external aids) [88:1204–14.") , 272:451–5.") , 286:1123–32.") , 291:329–34.") , 298 , 299 , 300 ], no auto-correction but asymmetric exercises [267:102–7.") , 274:82–4.") , 281 ], and no auto-correction and symmetric exercises [273:759–63.") , 276 , 292:396–402.") , 301 ]. Physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercise schools with some published evidence of efficacy (in alphabetical order) include FITS and DoboMed [277 , 291:329–34.") ], Global postural re-education [272:451–5.") ], Lyon 295 , 296 , [297 ], MedX [255 , 276 ], Schroth (either as Scoliosis Intensive Rehabilitation [192: an age- and sex-matched controlled study. Pediatr Rehabil. 2003;6(1):23–30.") , 279:35–40.") , 282:395–406.") ], or outpatient approach [190:209–14.") , 269:1429–35.") , 285 ]), SEAS [272:451–5.") , 275 ], and side-shift [278:406–10.") , 280 , 283 ]. However, the natural history of progression of scoliosis is still vastly unknown [48 , 302:270–7.") ]. It has been widely accepted that the probability of curve deterioration depends on patient age at diagnosis, type and severity of curve, sex and skeletal maturity [46 , 55:773–6.") , 303:2640–8.") ]. However, not all scolioses do progress. Literature suggests that 25 to 75% of diagnosed scoliosis curves remain unchanged, whereas 3 to 12% of curves spontaneously improve [26:173–6.") , 48 ]. Treatment decisions should be individualized, considering the probability of curve progression, based on curve magnitude, skeletal maturity, patient age and sexual maturity [11:2592–600.") , 56:1527–37.") ].

extraits.texte: Most recently, a high quality RCT by Schreiber et al. investigated the effect of 6-month Schroth intervention in combination with standard of care including observation and braces in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis and curves from 10° to 45°. Of 50 patients, 34 wore a brace (17 in each of the groups), mean age was 13.4 ± 1.6 years, and mean Cobb angle 28.5° ± 8.8°. The RCT showed that the Schroth intervention was superior compared to the standard of care alone in improving Cobb angles [319:234.") ], back muscle endurance [320 ], SRS-22r pain [320 ] and self-image domains [320 ]. In the intention-to-treat analysis, on average, the largest Cobb angle decreased by 1.2° in the Schroth and increased by 2.3° in the control group over 6 months, and this difference was statistically significant. When only completers were considered ( n = 44), this difference was even larger (4.1°) suggesting the importance of compliance with the treatment.

extraits.texte: The absolute goals for all patients in every clinical situation are to avoid fusion surgery.
Recently, a multi-centre RCT demonstrated that bracing is effective at preventing progression to the surgical range (defined as ≥ 50°)

Recently, Weinstein et al. [87:681.") ] performed a randomized controlled study, but the trial was stopped early owing to the efficacy of bracing, the rate of treatment success was 72% after bracing, as compared with 48% after observation. The authors concluded that bracing significantly decreased the progression of high-risk curves to the threshold for surgery in patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. This study is in contrast with results [189:S91–100.") ] of a systematic review published earlier by Dolan. The systematic review included only studies written in English, if observation or a TLSO was evaluated and if the sample closely matched the current indications for bracing (skeletal immaturity, age 15 years or less, Cobb angle between 20° and 45°). Eighteen studies were included (3 observation only, 15 bracing). Despite some uniformity in surgical indications, the surgical rates were extremely variable, ranging from 1 to 43% after bracing, and from 13 to 28% after observation. When pooled, the bracing surgical rate was 23% compared with 22% in the observation group. It was concluded that, based on the evidence presented, one could not recommend one approach over the other to prevent the need for surgery in AIS. The use of bracing relative to observation was said to be supported by “troublingly inconsistent or inconclusive studies of any level”. The article inclusion criteria used by Dolan resulted in the exclusion of some retrospective bracing studies, since they had used exercises together with bracing 190 , 191 , [192: an age- and sex-matched controlled study. Pediatr Rehabil. 2003;6(1):23–30.") ]. Studies having used exercises and bracing are summarized here.

extraits.texte: Finally, another important factor is the quality of bracing. There is good agreement to judge it according to the in-brace correction [136:537–45.") , 210:1343–52.") , 212:201–7.") , 229 , 230 , 231 , 232 , 233 , 234 ], even though the currently reported percentages of correction, showed a significant variability from 20 to 25% to 40–50%. Furthermore, the in brace correction is considered as prognostic factors for final good results and it has become, on one hand, the starting point to develop new braces [85 concept. Scoliosis. 2011;6:8.") , 202 , 203 , 235 , 236 , 237 , 237 , 238 , 239:180–5.") ] and, on the other, a biomechanical reference for various studies [232:1706–13.") , 239 , 240 , 241:339–44.") ]. Recently, a finite element model study confirmed the importance of immediate in-brace correction to predict long-term outcome of bracing treatment [242:369–76.") ]. Other factors such as the absolute reduction of the Cobb angle (i.e. in rigid curves over 50°) or 3D correction might also be important and should be considered in the future [243:185–90.") ]: in fact, it is still possible that a great in-brace reduction corresponds to a worsening of other parameters, e.g. in the sagittal plane, finally driving to a flat-back and worse functional results [133 , 146:213–20.") ] . In this respect, it is mandatory not to confuse the in-brace correction with the success of an orthotic treatment. While in-brace correction studies should be considered preliminary, only results at the end of treatment and/or at minimum of 1–2 years post treatment follow-up should be regarded as proof of efficacy. In any case, according to the actual knowledge, in-brace correction should be regarded as a way to individually judge the quality of the brace applied to single patients.

extraits.texte: The sagittal profile of the spine is frequently modified in scoliosis patients, and sagittal profile monitoring is advisable when considering all the correlations found between sagittal unbalance and disability or pain in adults with spinal deformities. The plumb line imbalance and the distance from the apical spinous process of the primary curve to the plumb line may be used for clinical evaluation, for clinical follow-up and also for the physiotherapeutic specific exercises effectiveness evaluation [446 ], as it is easy, quick, and reliable.

extraits.texte: Adherence to treatment is the second main issue to be considered. Many studies have underlined that reported compliance is correlated with final results [106 , 207:1957–63.") , 210:1343–52.") , 212:201–7.") , 213:151–8.") ]. Compliance to bracing has been correlated to quality of life and psychological issues [174:57–63.") , 214 , 215 , 216 , 217:257–61.") ]. Since patients during clinical evaluations overstate their adherence to treatment [218:143–6.") ], heat sensors have been developed to check real compliance: it has been confirmed that both reported and estimated hours of brace wearing are inaccurate 218 , 219 , 220 , 221 , 222 , 223 , [224:59–73.") ] and that compliance is not correlated with the hours of bracing prescribed [223:2070–4. discussion 2074") ]. Nighttime wear is more accepted than daytime [225:2243–50. discussion 2250–1") ], and a “dose-response” to bracing seems to be confirmed [210:1343–52.") , 226:343–7.") ]. It has also been proposed that it is possible to develop a progression model in single patients with a formula including the risk of progression at the beginning of brace treatment, plus the use in terms of brace tightness and wear time [222 ]. It is clear that, since patients are not fully compliant, bracing appears not effective. SOSORT propose that compliance should be considered in terms of management of patients: in this perspective, adherence to treatment is a characteristic neither of the treatment only, nor of the patient alone, but of the good interaction between these two factors, based on the active approach by an expert treatment team able to reduce the burden of the brace and increase the coping abilities of the patient [135. Guidelines on “standards of management of idiopathic scoliosis with corrective braces in everyday clinics and in clinical research”: SOSORT consensus 2008. Scoliosis. 2009;4:2.") , 227:107–11.") ]. A setting with great attention to the patient and his family and a team approach is able to enhance compliance, thus allowing very good adherence even with fulltime brace wear as demonstrated by research based on the use of compliance monitor [228:12.") ]. Mainly for these reasons, SOSORT proposes its recommendations [120 ].

extraits.texte: It seems as though patients with scoliosis are more likely to participate in sports like gymnastics [359:231–6.") , 360:751–5.") ]. It is thought that this is because patients with scoliosis tend to have a higher prevalence of joint laxity than the general population making them more flexible [345:663–6.") ]. There is a 10-fold higher incidence of scoliosis among rhythmic gymnasts [361:1367–72.") ], and a delayed menarche and generalized joint laxity are common in this population. Similarly, an increased incidence of scoliosis has been reported in ballet dancers (24%) [362:1348–53.") ], and a separate etiology for ballet and rhythmic gymnastics than in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis has been hypothesized [363 ]. However, in a pair of high-level 13.5-year-old female synchronized swimmers who were also monozygotic twins, only one presented with a 32° thoracolumbar curve. Therefore, it has been implied that factors other than genetics and participation in sport activities play an important role in development of scoliosis [364 twins discordant for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. Spine. 2008;33(17):E607–10.") ].

extraits.texte: For example it was reported that swimming, which has traditionally been recommended as a good sport activity for scoliosis (and even prescribed by some physicians as a treatment), is associated with an increased risk of trunk asymmetries and hyperkyphosis [365:163–7.") ]. In addition, in an old study conducted in 1983, Becker screened 336 competitive adolescent swimmers for scoliosis and found prevalence of scoliosis to be 6.9% [366:149–58.") ]. This number seems high, but there is no evidence to suggest that swimming is a causative factor of scoliosis. There is a paucity of correlational research in the area of scoliosis and asymmetric sports, traditionally blamed for causing scoliosis. In addition, in a recent cross-sectional study by Zaina et al., tennis was found not to be correlated with spine deformities [367 ].

#### Going home

Length of stay in hospital may vary and will depend on a number of factors:

* Your medical team are happy for discharge
* Your pain being controlled on oral medication
* You are independently mobile, and your physiotherapist is happy you are safe to go home
* Length of stay may vary but is often between 4-5 days

An outpatient clinic appointment will be made for you to see the specialist spinal nurse in clinic usually 6 weeks post op.

You will be reviewed in consultant clinic approximately 3 months post-surgery.
